precepts.why:
The Lord told Ezekiel, “set thy face against mount Seir, and prophesy against it.” Who or what is mount Seir? Now there is context, and no one can say we are making it up. We don't need a cosigner; the Bible says what it says.

With that key, Ezekiel 35 opens up. “Because thou hast had a perpetual hatred”: a hatred that has gone on for centuries, from Esau their father to his children toward us. It is in their blood to hate us; their hatred is damn near biological, from the womb to the tomb. That is why they do such terrible things to us: eating us, hanging us, castrating us, raping us, mutilating us. A sister whose husband was murdered sought justice in court; they hung her from a tree, shot her full of holes, cut the unborn baby out of her, stepped on its head and set it on fire. Damn! That is a perfect hatred. There's no record of black folks ever doing that to white folks. What we did to the French in Haiti was retaliation, and they deserved it; she was innocent.

They shed our blood “in the time that their iniquity had an end”: after the Emancipation Proclamation came the KKK, Black Codes, Jim Crow, convict leasing and redlining. That envy goes back to the birthright. Esau was the firstborn and felt it was not fair that God chose Jacob, and the Lord says he will do “according to thine anger, and according to thine envy.”

Edom said, “These two nations and these two countries shall be mine, and we will possess it.” The two nations are Judah and Israel; the two countries were Judea and Samaria and later Israel and the Americas. They took one as Romans and later as Israelis, and the other as Christians, as conquistadors. “I have heard all thy blasphemies”: this is a direct precept to Revelation 2:9 and 3:9, the blasphemy of them which say they are Jews and are not, possessing the land and professing to be the people that belong there. They have said it to our faces: yes, you are the real Jews, but the land is ours now. They know; the world does not.

“When the whole earth rejoiceth, I will make thee desolate.” As long as that nation is on the earth, there can be no peace; when there is no more Edom, the earth rejoices. “thou shalt be desolate, O mount Seir, and all Idumea, even all of it.” The judgment on Edom is complete, with no exceptions, and they shall know that he is the Lord.
